title: Study Finds How a High-Calorie Diet May Affect the Brain
paragraphs: It is well known that eating a lot of high-calorie food can lead to weight gain and health problems such as diabetes. However, scientists are still trying to understand exactly how such diets may also affect the brain. Now, a team of researchers in Japan believes it has discovered one possible explanation.

The study was led by Professor Hitoshi Okazawa and Associate Professor Hikari Tanaka of the Institute of Science Tokyo, together with researchers from other universities in Japan and the United States. It was published in the journal Molecular Psychiatry in September 2026.

The researchers fed mice a high-fat diet for one or six weeks and then examined their brains. They found that the diet reduced the levels of a protein called PQBP1 in the cerebral cortex, a part of the brain that plays an important role in thinking and memory. This protein helps control a process called RNA splicing, which affects how genes are used to make proteins.

When the levels of PQBP1 fell, the splicing of several genes related to synapses, the connections between nerve cells, was changed. These changes were linked to problems in the structure and function of synapses, as well as to poorer cognitive abilities in the mice.

The researchers then tried to reverse these effects. When they gave the mice pioglitazone, a drug that is used to treat diabetes, the levels of PQBP1 were restored. This also improved the mice's synapses and cognitive abilities. A type of gene therapy that restored PQBP1 had similar positive effects.

According to Okazawa, the findings reveal a molecular pathway that links a high-calorie diet to cognitive impairment. The researchers believe this pathway could become a target for new treatments in the future.

However, it is important to note that the study was carried out on mice, not humans. Further research will be needed to find out whether the same process happens in the human brain, and whether these findings could lead to treatments for people.
